items.title: CVE-2026-76461: Cisco Cisco Secure Email Gateway SQL Injection Vulnerability
items.one_liner: An unauthenticated remote SQL injection vulnerability in Cisco Secure Email Gateway allows root command execution and is now listed on CISA KEV.
items.summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-76461 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw involves a SQL injection in Cisco AsyncOS for Cisco Secure Email Gateway (SEG). An unauthenticated, remote attacker can exploit it to execute arbitrary commands with root privileges on the underlying operating system. Federal agencies are mandated to apply vendor mitigations or discontinue product use by September 17, 2026.
key_facts: Target product: Cisco Secure Email Gateway (AsyncOS)
Impact: Unauthenticated remote root command execution
items.bottom_line: Organizations running Cisco Secure Email Gateway must immediately apply vendor mitigations or discontinue use before the September 17, 2026 federal deadline.

claims.support_span: Cisco AsyncOS software for Cisco Secure Email Gateway (SEG) contains a SQL injection vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands with root privileges on the underlying operating system.

items.title: CVE-2026-78006 (CRITICAL 9.8): The The Events Calendar plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, an…
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-78006 allows unauthenticated remote code execution in The Events Calendar WordPress plugin versions up to 6.17.4.
items.summary: A critical unauthenticated Remote Code Execution flaw (CVE-2026-78006, CVSS 9.8) has been identified in The Events Calendar WordPress plugin affecting all versions up to 6.17.4. The vulnerability exists within the is_safe_widget_instance function, where PHP magic method pre-parsing and an integrity forging flaw in enable_rendering_widget_copied() allow arbitrary deserialization. Attackers can exploit this without prior authentication by submitting a comment containing block markup on event pages, as WordPress moderation-hash URLs render pending comments immediately.
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated attackers can achieve full remote code execution on WordPress sites running The Events Calendar <= 6.17.4 by submitting event comments.

claims.text: The Events Calendar plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthenticated remote code execution in versions up to 6.17.4.
claims.support_span: The The Events Calendar plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, and including, 6.17.4 via the is_safe_widget_instance function.

claims.text: The vulnerability is assigned a critical CVSS base score of 9.8.
claims.support_span: CVSS base score 9.8 (CRITICAL).

claims.text: Exploitation relies on WordPress moderation-hash URLs that evaluate block markup in pending event comments before approval.
claims.support_span: This is exploitable without authentication or approval because the plugin's V2 single-event template runs do_blocks() over buffered comment HTML, and WordPress returns a moderation-hash URL that allows an unauthenticated commenter to immediately view their own pending comment, delivering the injected block markup to the vulnerable code path before any moderation occurs.

items.title: CVE-2026-0298 GlobalProtect App: Code Execution Vulnerability in Windows Pre-Logon Access Provider (PLAP) (Severity: MEDIUM)
items.one_liner: GlobalProtect Windows clients using SAML CBL are vulnerable to local SYSTEM code execution via PLAP input validation flaws.
items.summary: An improper input validation vulnerability exists in the Windows Pre-Logon Access Provider component of the Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect app, enabling a man-in-the-middle attacker to execute arbitrary code with SYSTEM privileges. The flaw affects specific version ranges of the 6.0, 6.2, and 6.3 branches on Windows when configured to use SAML authentication with the Connect Before Logon feature. Palo Alto Networks has issued updates and workaround guidance, noting no active exploitation at the time of disclosure.
items.bottom_line: Palo Alto GlobalProtect Windows users leveraging SAML with Connect Before Logon face a local SYSTEM code execution risk via MITM manipulation.

items.title: CVE-2026-78175 (HIGH 8.8): The Tutor LMS – eLearning and online course solution plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injecti…
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-78175 in Tutor LMS WordPress plugin enables remote code execution via PHP object injection.
items.summary: A PHP Object Injection vulnerability, CVE-2026-78175, has been discovered in the Tutor LMS WordPress plugin in versions up to and including 4.0.7. The vulnerability exists within the withdraw_method_field parameter of the tutor_save_withdraw_account AJAX handler, which lacks role checks and relies solely on a nonce. Exploitation allows authenticated users with subscriber-level access and above—or unauthenticated attackers when user registration is enabled—to trigger a GuzzleHttp POP chain via the plugin's bundled PayPal Composer autoloader, resulting in remote code execution. The vulnerability is rated high severity with a CVSS score of 8.8.
key_facts: Affected product: Tutor LMS WordPress plugin through 4.0.7
items.bottom_line: Unsecured AJAX handlers in WordPress plugins can lead to remote code execution through PHP object injection and insecure POP chains.

items.title: CVE-2026-75800 (CRITICAL 9.8): The Frontegg SAML SSO WordPress plugin through 1.0.1 does not verify the signature or issuer of SAML authenti…
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-75800 is a critical SAML SSO authentication bypass flaw in the Frontegg WordPress plugin allowing unauthenticated admin access.
items.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability, CVE-2026-75800, affects the Frontegg SAML SSO WordPress plugin through version 1.0.1. The flaw stems from the plugin's failure to verify the signature or issuer of SAML authentication responses prior to establishing a user session. This allows unauthenticated attackers to log in as any user, including administrators, and create arbitrary accounts. The vulnerability carries a CVSS base score of 9.8.

items.bottom_line: Frontegg SAML SSO WordPress plugin versions up to 1.0.1 allow unauthenticated full account takeover due to missing SAML signature verification.

items.title: Non-Zero-Day VPN Flaw Left Japan ‘s Government Shared Network Platform Exposed: 246,000 Records at Risk
items.one_liner: A VPN vulnerability exposed 246,000 Japanese government records across 23 ministries and agencies.
items.summary: Japan's Digital Agency disclosed that attackers exploited a medium-severity VPN vulnerability to compromise the Government Solution Service (GSS) network, potentially leaking personal data belonging to approximately 246,000 government employees, public officials, and contractors. The breach was detected on June 25, confirmed as VPN exploitation on July 9, and publicly disclosed 78 days after initial detection. An outsider leveraged the VPN flaw, used a maintenance and operations staff member's account to access the server, and browsed numerous files. The leaked information includes names, email addresses, phone numbers, and physical addresses, though it excludes My Number identification numbers and financial details.
items.bottom_line: Unpatched or exploited VPN devices can directly compromise shared government network infrastructure and leak hundreds of thousands of internal personnel records.

items.title: Hacked HBO Max Reddit Account Used for Malware Delivery via ClickFix Attack
items.one_liner: Attackers hijacked the verified HBO Max Reddit account to distribute MacSync, AMOS Helper, and clipboard hijackers via ClickFix lures.
items.summary: Threat actors compromised the official HBO Max Reddit account to run 108 malicious advertisements in a 48-hour malvertising campaign named PasteSwitch. The ads directed users to a spoofed domain pushing a fake macOS native application using ClickFix social engineering lures that instructed victims to run malicious commands in Terminal or PowerShell. The attack delivered infostealers including MacSync, AMOS Helper, and Amatera Stealer to extract credentials and crypto wallets, while deploying persistent clipboard replacers to redirect crypto payments. Reddit has suspended the compromised advertising account.
key_facts: Compromised asset: Official u/hbomax Reddit account
Malware families: MacSync, AMOS Helper, Amatera Stealer, AnimateClipper, ZigClipper
Attack technique: ClickFix terminal execution prompts
items.bottom_line: Threat actors are weaponizing verified social media brand accounts to deliver cross-platform info-stealers and cryptocurrency clippers via ClickFix terminal execution prompts.

On Windows, the attack relied on MSHTA and PowerShell to deliver the Amatera Stealer and achieve persistence.

items.title: Revolut gave customer IDs and financial data to a government impostor
items.one_liner: Revolut disclosed customer passports, selfies, and banking statements to a fraudster who sent bogus requests from a legitimate government email domain.
items.summary: Financial platform Revolut confirmed that sensitive customer data was handed over to a fraudster who impersonated a government agency using a legitimate government email domain. The social engineering incident did not breach internal systems or compromise customer balances, but resulted in the unauthorized disclosure of passport copies, driver's licenses, verification selfies, contact details, and transaction histories for a limited group of users. Revolut blocked the fraudulent sender address and notified regulators, while advising affected customers to monitor for secondary identity theft and social engineering scams.
key_facts: Breach vector: Social engineering via legitimate government email domain
Compromised data: Passport copies, driver's licenses, verification selfies, transaction histories
items.bottom_line: Revolut customer identity documents, verification selfies, and transaction histories were leaked via a social engineering request originating from an authenticated government email address.

items.title: CVE-2026-86792: Apache Airflow Apache Kafka provider: Connection-editor remote code execution on the Scheduler via Kafka connection callback configuration
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-86792 allows Airflow connection editors to achieve RCE on the scheduler via unsafe Kafka provider configuration callbacks.
items.summary: A moderate-severity remote code execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-86792, has been discovered in the Apache Airflow Apache Kafka provider versions 1.15.0 through 2.0.0. The flaw occurs because the provider resolves dotted-path strings found in a Kafka connection's extra field into Python callables via import_string without an allowlist, handing them to the confluent-kafka client. In deployments where the Kafka event producer is enabled, a user with permissions only to edit Airflow connections can achieve arbitrary code execution on the scheduler process rather than being restricted to workers. Users are advised to upgrade to version 2.0.0 or later, which introduces a necessary allowlist configuration.
key_facts: Affected: Apache Airflow Kafka provider 1.15.0 up to 2.0.0
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated or low-privilege Airflow connection editors can achieve control-plane code execution on the scheduler if unsafe Kafka provider callbacks are enabled.

items.title: AGENTQ: Quantization-Conditioned Backdoor Attacks on LLM Agents
items.one_liner: This research exposes a critical supply-chain risk where quantized LLM agents can be weaponized post-deployment, bypassing standard safety checks.
items.summary: Researchers have identified a new threat vector called Quantization-Conditioned Backdoor Attacks (QCA) against LLM agents. The attack involves releasing a full-precision model that passes safety audits but triggers malicious behavior once quantized for deployment. The proposed 'AGENTQ' framework demonstrates that these backdoors can be injected with minimal impact on benign utility, highlighting the need for quantization-aware safety evaluations.
items.bottom_line: Quantization-conditioned attacks allow adversaries to hide malicious payloads in LLM agents that only activate after the model is quantized for deployment.

items.title: BadEngram: Backdoor Attack on Gated Memory Components in LLMs
items.one_liner: BadEngram demonstrates that backdoor attacks can successfully compromise gated parametric memory modules in LLMs while leaving backbone weights intact.
items.summary: Researchers have uncovered BadEngram, a post-training backdoor attack targeting gated parametric memory components in large language models. These modular memory components, used in modern models to expand capacity without scaling computation, form a vulnerable independent attack surface since their parameters can be modified separately from the backbone weights. In controlled tests, BadEngram achieved a 96.6% Attack Success Rate (ASR) on triggered inputs while keeping clean accuracy at 99.6% and false activation below 0.1%. Furthermore, scaling tests on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next demonstrated that the attack achieved 50.4% ASR on HarmBench and 60.0% on AdvBench, proving that gated memory parameters represent a critical security threat whose integrity cannot be assured by an unmodified backbone.
items.bottom_line: LLM gated memory components present an independent attack surface that can be backdoored to bypass safety guardrails without altering the base model weights.

claims.text: We introduce BadEngram, a post-training attack that exploits this surface to implant persistent, trigger-dependent behavior while leaving conventional backbone weights and the execution graph unchanged.
claims.support_span: We introduce BadEngram, a post-training attack that exploits this surface to implant persistent, trigger-dependent behavior while leaving conventional backbone weights and the execution graph unchanged.

claims.text: We first establish the attack's feasibility and causally characterize its mechanism in a controlled Engram model, where BadEngram achieves 96.6% ASR on triggered inputs while limiting false activation on matched trigger-free inputs to 0.1% and preserving 99.6% clean accuracy.

items.title: Cisco UCS and UCS-Based Appliances UEFI Shell Secure Boot Bypass Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A critical UEFI Secure Boot bypass in Cisco UCS hardware allows attackers to execute unauthorized code at the preboot level.
items.summary: Cisco has disclosed a vulnerability in the UEFI Shell implementation of its UCS servers and appliances that allows attackers to bypass Secure Boot. By utilizing memory write commands available in the UEFI Shell, an attacker with physical access or valid credentials can manipulate preboot variables to execute unauthorized software. Cisco has released software updates to address this flaw, and there are no available workarounds.
key_facts: Affected: Cisco UCS Servers and appliances
items.bottom_line: Administrators must patch Cisco UCS firmware immediately to prevent attackers from compromising the boot process and gaining persistent control.

items.title: ZDI-26-684: Linux Kernel KSMBD Query Directory Request Race Condition Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.one_liner: Linux kernel KSMBD race condition ZDI-26-684 allows unauthenticated remote code execution.
items.summary: A critical remote code execution vulnerability, ZDI-26-684, has been identified in the Linux kernel's KSMBD server implementation due to a race condition. The flaw exists within the handling of dir_fp objects where operations lack proper object locking during query directory requests. Unauthenticated remote attackers can exploit this race condition to execute arbitrary code with full kernel privileges on systems with KSMBD enabled. Linux developers have released a specific code commit to fix the synchronization bug.
items.bottom_line: Administrators exposing the KSMBD file server module must update their Linux kernels immediately to prevent unauthenticated remote code execution.

items.one_liner: If your mobile or media-processing stack uses stb_vorbis, you are vulnerable to memory corruption via malicious audio files.
items.summary: A heap buffer overflow vulnerability, CVE-2026-89266, has been identified in the stb_vorbis library up to version 1.22. Attackers can exploit this by providing a maliciously crafted Ogg Vorbis file to trigger out-of-bounds writes, leading to heap corruption or process crashes.

items.title: VMs won't contain cyber-capable agents
items.one_liner: Testing showed that an advanced AI cyber agent could autonomously escape a QEMU/KVM virtual machine multiple times.
items.summary: Trail of Bits evaluated the cyber capabilities of GPT 5.6-Cyber by tasking it with escaping a QEMU/KVM virtual machine running on a Debian Linux host. The AI agent successfully escaped the virtual machine three separate times by exploiting unpatched host kernel bugs, recently disclosed vulnerabilities, and discovering zero-day flaws in QEMU dependencies. Operating autonomously for hours, the agent pulled research papers, wrote exploits, and navigated system hurdles with minimal human intervention. The experiment demonstrates that standard virtual machines cannot safely contain sufficiently advanced AI cyber agents.
key_facts: Host environment: Debian Linux 12, AMD Zen3
items.bottom_line: Standard virtual machine isolation is insufficient to contain advanced AI agents capable of autonomous vulnerability discovery and exploit development.

items.title: US 10-year Treasury yield rises to highest since 2007 as Fed rate hike bets strengthen
items.one_liner: US 10-year Treasury yields hit a 2007 high of 5.041% as crude spikes and Fed rate hike bets strengthen.
items.summary: The US 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.041 percent on September 15, hitting its highest level since July 2007, driven by surging crude oil prices and increasing expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike. Brent crude futures briefly touched $110 per barrel as ongoing conflict in the Middle East disrupted fuel flows and closed the Strait of Hormuz. The combination of high borrowing costs and elevated energy expenses threatens to squeeze corporate spending, investment plans, and household budgets. Despite US Treasury buyback operations, bond investors remain concerned over stubbornly high inflation exceeding the Federal Reserve's 2 percent target.
key_facts: Yield peak comparison: Highest since July 2007
items.bottom_line: Spiking crude oil prices and stubborn inflation are pushing benchmark US bond yields to multi-year highs and increasing borrowing pressures globally.

items.title: BambooToken Malware Uses MQTT to Control Windows and Linux Systems
items.one_liner: BambooToken malware targets Windows and Linux systems via MQTT communications, leveraging DLL sideloading in Tendyron financial tokens.
items.summary: Security researchers have detailed a multi-platform malware campaign active since February 2023 that targets Windows and Linux systems across Asia and South America using the MQTT protocol for command-and-control (C2). Codenamed BambooToken, the malware relies on DLL sideloading vulnerabilities in Tendyron's 'OnKey' software—a hardware-based PKI token used in financial and government sectors with over 190 million units in circulation—to trigger execution within secure environments. While Tendyron's certificates remain uncompromised, attackers exploit local binaries to load rogue DLLs that harvest system details, receive remote plug-in commands via MQTT, and communicate with C2 servers. Most samples have been uploaded from Chinese IP addresses, pointing to a targeted regional data collection effort.
key_facts: Affected hardware token: Tendyron OnKey (190 million in circulation)
items.bottom_line: Attackers are abusing DLL sideloading vulnerabilities in widely deployed Tendyron security tokens to execute BambooToken, a multi-platform MQTT-controlled backdoor.

items.title: One Exploit Chain, Two Espionage Campaigns: Chrome and Windows Under Fire
items.one_liner: Two Chinese APT groups exploited a Chrome/Windows zero-day chain by capitalizing on the patch gap between upstream Chromium fixes and stable browser releases.
items.summary: Two China-linked threat actors, UTA0560 and JungleBamboo (APT31), exploited a zero-day exploit chain targeting Google Chrome and Windows starting September 1, 2026. The multi-stage attack leveraged a Chrome type-confusion vulnerability (CVE-2026-85046) in the V8 sandbox, a WebAssembly defect (CVE-2026-87491) to escape the sandbox, and a Windows kernel flaw (CVE-2026-85880) to inject code into the main browser process via a compromised university website. Although a patch for CVE-2026-85046 had landed in the open-source Chromium repository upstream after being reported on August 4, 2026, Google Chrome had not yet shipped the fix, creating a critical patch gap exploited in the wild. Once code execution was achieved, UTA0560 deployed the in-memory GRIMWEDGE backdoor, while JungleBamboo installed a malicious Chrome extension (LONGTALE) disguised as a Google Gemini assistant to harvest credentials and log keystrokes.
key_facts: CVE-2026-85046: Chrome V8 type confusion vulnerability
items.bottom_line: Attackers weaponized an upstream Chromium fix before Google shipped it, using a three-bug exploit chain to deploy distinct espionage payloads.

items.title: Texas Utility CenterPoint Energy Confirms Breach After Hacker Leaks Data
items.one_liner: CenterPoint Energy confirms a data breach impacting customer personal information following a hacker's leak on a cybercrime forum.
items.summary: Texas utility provider CenterPoint Energy confirmed an unauthorized third party obtained personal customer information through an external-facing system, following claims by a hacker on a cybercrime forum who leaked a 2.5 GB archive file. The threat actor alleged the theft of roughly 7.5 million records and threatened further attacks on core infrastructure if demands weren't met. CenterPoint stated that utility delivery operations remain unaffected and do not expect a material impact from the breach. The company has previously faced multiple third-party data exposure claims linked to historical ransomware campaigns.
key_facts: Customers impacted: roughly 7 million across Indiana, Minnesota, Ohio, and Texas
items.bottom_line: An external system compromise at CenterPoint Energy exposes personal customer records, underscoring ongoing cybersecurity vulnerabilities in major public utilities.

items.title: LiteSpeed Enterprise Flaw Could Let One Hosting Account Gain Root Access on a Shared Server
items.one_liner: A critical unpatched root escalation vulnerability in LiteSpeed Enterprise threatens shared hosting environments, requiring manual intervention outside standard auto-updates.
items.summary: A critical privilege-escalation vulnerability in LiteSpeed Web Server Enterprise (versions prior to 6.3.7) allows low-privilege website users to gain root access on shared-hosting servers, bypassing isolation mechanisms like CloudLinux's CageFS. cPanel warned administrators about the flaw in a September 14 advisory and urged manual updates using a specific command because automatic updates may be delayed. Neither company has disclosed exact details of the exploit mechanism, CVE identifiers, or severity scores, though LiteSpeed included three unlisted security changes in version 6.3.7. This follows two earlier actively exploited privilege-escalation flaws reported in LiteSpeed's cPanel user-end plugin in May and June 2026.
key_facts: Affected versions: LiteSpeed Web Server Enterprise before 6.3.7
Previous related CVEs: CVE-2026-48172 and CVE-2026-54420
items.bottom_line: Shared hosting administrators must manually force a LiteSpeed upgrade to version 6.3.7 immediately to prevent low-privilege users from achieving root access.

items.title: 'Sandworm' Chains Cisco Vulnerabilities to Deploy Cyclops Blink
items.one_liner: Sandworm is actively using critical Cisco FMC vulnerabilities to deploy a modernized, Linux-native version of the Cyclops Blink botnet.
items.summary: The Russian threat actor Sandworm is actively exploiting two vulnerabilities in Cisco's Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) to deploy a new, upgraded variant of the Cyclops Blink botnet. The attack chain leverages CVE-2026-20079, a critical authentication bypass, and CVE-2026-20316 to gain root access and install a reverse shell. This new variant has shifted from 32-bit PowerPC to 64-bit x86-64 Linux, enabling broader targeting and adding capabilities for packet capture and network scanning. Cisco has released hotfixes and advises immediate patching due to confirmed exploitation in the wild.
key_facts: Malware: Cyclops Blink (new x86-64 Linux variant)
items.bottom_line: Organizations using Cisco Secure FMC must apply the available hotfixes immediately to prevent root-level compromise and persistent botnet infection.

items.title: Maximum Severity GitLab Flaw Puts Supply Chains at Risk
items.one_liner: Threat actors are actively exploiting critical GitLab path traversal flaw CVE-2026-85706 to exfiltrate SSH configs and CI/CD secrets.
items.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting CVE-2026-85706, a maximum-severity 10.0 CVSS path traversal vulnerability in GitLab Community and Enterprise Editions caused by improper path confinement and missing authentication in the repository commits API. Disclosed and patched by GitLab on September 10, the flaw permits unauthenticated users to read arbitrary files from self-hosted servers. Following CISA's directive ordering federal agencies to patch or disable affected instances, security vendor watchTowr observed rapid escalation over the weekend, with attackers exfiltrating configuration files, system SSH credentials, and CI/CD secrets to pivot into downstream enterprise infrastructure.
items.bottom_line: Active exploitation of critical GitLab CVE-2026-85706 allows unauthenticated attackers to steal system secrets and compromise software supply chains.

items.title: Human Attacker Exploits Marimo RCE, Reaches SSH Bastion in Eight Seconds
items.one_liner: A skilled human attacker manually exploited a Marimo RCE vulnerability to pivot to an SSH bastion in eight seconds, matching AI-agent speed.
items.summary: In an incident illustrating that skilled human operators can move at machine speeds without AI agents, a threat actor pivoted from a vulnerable Marimo notebook instance to an AWS-backed SSH bastion host in just eight seconds. The operator exploited CVE-2026-39987, a pre-authenticated remote code execution vulnerability (CVSS score 9.3) in Marimo, writing and debugging custom Python scripts entirely by hand. Over a nine-hour interactive session comprising more than 850 commands, the attacker extracted AWS credentials via AWS Secrets Manager and authenticated to the bastion host without relying on automated offensive agent frameworks. Meanwhile, separate findings revealed a cryptomining campaign compromising over 3,500 Redis servers using SLAVEOF command smuggling, AOF-based SSH key injection, and Lua sandbox escapes.
key_facts: CVE-2026-39987: Marimo pre-authenticated RCE vulnerability, CVSS 9.3
items.bottom_line: Skilled human operators can execute complex credential-pivoting attacks at machine speed without AI assistance, successfully weaponizing critical RCE flaws like Marimo's CVE-2026-39987.

items.title: CVE-2026-0308 PAN-OS: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Vulnerability in the Web Interface (Severity: LOW)
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-0308 is a low-severity stored XSS vulnerability in Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS web interface allowing authenticated admin script execution.
items.summary: A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0308 with a LOW severity rating (CVSS 4.8), affects Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS software on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls as well as Panorama virtual and M-Series appliances. The flaw enables a malicious authenticated administrator to store and execute arbitrary JavaScript payloads using the web interface. Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are unaffected, and Palo Alto Networks is unaware of any malicious exploitation. Administrators can mitigate the risk by restricting management interface access to a secure jump box or by enabling specific Threat Prevention signatures.

items.title: Iran war has led to US munitions shortfalls, Pentagon inspector confirms
items.one_liner: A Pentagon inspector general report confirms strategic U.S. munitions shortfalls from the Iran conflict, directly contradicting White House claims.
items.summary: A U.S. Defense Department inspector general report confirms that ongoing military operations against Iran have caused strategic inventory shortfalls in munitions and resupply bottlenecks, contradicting President Donald Trump's claims of virtually unlimited ammunition. The independent watchdog revealed that the U.S. spent over $22 billion on munitions between February and June, contributing to total war expenditures of $33.4 billion, while equipment losses include advanced aircraft and numerous drones. The White House rejected the findings, maintaining that military stockpiles are more than sufficient. Meanwhile, a separate Congressional Budget Office estimate placed the total cost of the conflict even higher at $38 billion.
key_facts: Equipment losses: 4 F-15e jets, 1 F-35 fighter, 30 MQ-9 drones
items.bottom_line: High-intensity operations against Iran have severely depleted U.S. missile and munition stockpiles, creating industrial bottlenecks that challenge official claims of unlimited supplies.

items.title: CVE-2026-79993: Apache ZooKeeper: Missing ACL check on deleteContainer opcode allows unauthorized deletion of any empty persistent/container znode
items.one_liner: Unauthenticated TCP clients can delete arbitrary empty ZooKeeper znodes via an unvalidated deleteContainer opcode.
items.summary: A critical vulnerability designated CVE-2026-79993 affects Apache ZooKeeper versions 3.8.0 through 3.8.6 and 3.9.0 through 3.9.5 due to a missing ACL check on the internal deleteContainer opcode (0x14/20). Unauthenticated attackers who can open a plain TCP session on port 2181 can issue the raw protocol command to delete any empty persistent, container, or TTL znode, bypassing standard session and delete ACL validations. Users must upgrade immediately to patched versions 3.8.7 or 3.9.6 to close the authorization bypass.
items.bottom_line: Upgrade Apache ZooKeeper to 3.8.7 or 3.9.6 to patch an unauthenticated znode deletion vulnerability.

claims.text: Users should upgrade to ZooKeeper version 3.9.6 or 3.8.7 to fix the issue.

items.title: CVE-2026-60163: MySQL Group Replication unauthenticated remote arbitrary SQL execution
items.one_liner: This is a high-impact remote code execution vulnerability in database replication that requires immediate patching or configuration review.
items.summary: Oracle has disclosed a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-60163, in MySQL Group Replication that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary SQL commands. The flaw exists in the XCom replication listener, where incoming messages from non-members are incorrectly processed as valid member proposals. While initially rated as a local issue, the attack surface can be fully remote depending on the group_replication_ip_allowlist configuration. Affected versions include MySQL Server 8.4.0–8.4.10 and 9.7.0–9.7.1, as well as various MySQL Cluster versions.
key_facts: CVE-2026-60163: Unauthenticated remote arbitrary SQL execution
Attack Vector: Adjacent Network (can be fully remote)
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated attackers can gain control over MySQL database instances by exploiting the Group Replication XCom stack.

items.title: ₹9 lakh crore gone in a day! Stock market selloff drive over 200 stocks to their 52-week lows
items.one_liner: A heavy selloff in Indian equities wipes out ₹9 lakh crore and drags over 200 stocks to 52-week lows.
items.summary: The Indian stock market suffered a broad, across-the-board selloff on Tuesday, September 15, dragging benchmark indices down by over 1% and mid- and small-cap segments down by more than 2%. The Sensex plunged 778 points to close at 74,003.82, while the Nifty 50 dropped 280 points to finish at 23,118.60, marking a second consecutive session of losses. The selloff wiped out ₹9 lakh crore in investor wealth as total market capitalization fell to ₹472.4 lakh crore, bringing 215 stocks—including major names like Reliance Industries, Bank of Baroda, and IRCTC—down to their 52-week lows.

items.bottom_line: Widespread market correction in Indian equities erodes trillions in market capitalization and drives numerous blue-chip stocks to yearly lows.

items.one_liner: A new diagnostic tool called the Consistency Analyzer identifies flip-prone decision points in LLM agent traces to halve task reliability gaps.
items.summary: LLM agent benchmarks often rely on average pass rates (Mean@k) that obscure significant execution variability across repeated runs. On AppWorld, a ReAct agent using GPT-4.1 achieved a 77.4% average success rate (Mean@5), but succeeded across all five repeated runs on only 53.0% of tasks—revealing a 24.4-point consistency gap. To target this unreliability, researchers developed the Consistency Analyzer, a diagnostic tool that resamples recorded trajectories to pinpoint flip-prone decision points without needing ground truth. Translating these diagnoses into automatically distilled guidelines halved the consistency gap from 24.4pp to 12.0pp without degrading average accuracy.
items.bottom_line: Measuring Pass^k alongside Mean@k exposes hidden agent unreliability, and targeted trajectory guidelines can effectively close the consistency gap.

items.title: Trustworthy Agentic AI: A Comprehensive Cybersecurity and Systems Survey on Threat Landscapes, Defense Architectures, and Open Challenges
items.one_liner: A comprehensive systems security survey outlines threat landscapes and a zero-trust defense-in-depth architecture for autonomous agentic AI.
items.summary: The transition of foundation models into autonomous agentic systems with recursive reasoning, persistent memory, and live tool execution dissolves classical security boundaries because natural language functions simultaneously as input data, control code, and communication protocols. To address this Turing-complete blast radius, a comprehensive systems-security survey formalizes agent architecture and establishes a six-dimensional trustworthiness taxonomy covering security, safety, privacy, explainability, fairness, and accountability. The study synthesizes 206 foundational works to propose a multi-layered zero-trust defense-in-depth architecture featuring Dual-LLM isolation, Capability-Based Access Control, kernel eBPF probes, and sandboxed runtimes.
items.bottom_line: Securing autonomous agentic systems requires moving beyond perimeter defenses to zero-trust architectures combining dual-LLM isolation, eBPF probes, and capability-based access control.

claims.text: This survey delivers a comprehensive systems-security reference framework for trustworthy agentic AI, synthesizing 206 foundational studies and regulatory standards.
claims.support_span: This survey delivers a comprehensive systems-security reference framework for trustworthy agentic AI, synthesizing 206 foundational studies and regulatory standards.

items.title: Misleading the Planner through Deceptive Resumes: Registration-Time Injection in Centralized Multi-Agent Systems
items.one_liner: Agentic systems are vulnerable to prompt injection via malicious worker descriptions, which can hijack the entire planning logic.
items.summary: Researchers have identified a registration-time injection vulnerability in centralized LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS). By manipulating worker-description fields, attackers can plant payloads that influence the planner's task decomposition and subtask assignment, even if the malicious agent is never invoked. The attack can significantly degrade system performance, increase token consumption, or divert task execution. The researchers proposed DescGuard, a defense mechanism that sanitizes worker-scoped interface information before it reaches the planner.
key_facts: Impact: Task success reduction from 84.31% to 37.25%
items.bottom_line: Trusting third-party agent descriptions in a centralized MAS allows attackers to manipulate the system's planning logic before any user interaction occurs.

items.title: SpliTEE: Improving LLM Inference on Trusted Hardware with Differentially Private GPU Outsourcing
items.one_liner: Differential privacy replaces encryption in split LLM inference between TEEs and GPUs, offering a faster, floating-point-safe alternative for secure processing.
items.summary: Researchers have extended split-inference architectures for Large Language Models to run securely on CPU-based Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) by replacing encryption with differential privacy to protect intermediate inputs sent to untrusted GPUs. The authors demonstrate that naive intermediate representations are vulnerable to prompt-reconstruction attacks that recover prompts with nearly 80% accuracy. By performing a global sensitivity analysis of key LLM functions, they bound the required scale of differentially private noise without requiring quantization, allowing models to remain in the floating-point domain. Implemented using Intel TDX and tested on Llama-3.2-3B and Qwen3-4B, the split execution runs nearly twice as fast as full CPU inference inside TDX and 5-15 seconds faster than encryption-based Slalom. This approach enables secure, efficient LLM inference while ensuring prompt reconstruction cannot recover more information than an unrelated prompt.
items.bottom_line: Differential privacy can replace encryption in split-inference TEE architectures to accelerate secure LLM execution without sacrificing privacy against prompt-reconstruction attacks.

items.title: Exploring Automated Vulnerability Identification in JavaScript Code Using Large Language Models
items.one_liner: Fine-tuned LLMs significantly outperform traditional SAST tools in detecting JavaScript vulnerabilities across multiple CWE categories.
items.summary: An empirical study evaluating large language models across 1,125 JavaScript code snippets reveals that LLMs substantially outperform traditional Static Application Security Testing tools in snippet-level vulnerability identification. Testing three model families—Gemini 1.5 Flash, GPT-4o Mini, and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B—across multiple prompting strategies and fine-tuning approaches, researchers found that fine-tuning improved detection accuracy from 29% to 60%. A fine-tuned Gemini 1.5 Flash model achieved the highest overall accuracy of 60%, compared to near-zero performance from rule-based analyzers. Performance varied by category, reaching up to 84% accuracy on structured flaws like SQL injection.
items.bottom_line: Task-aligned fine-tuning enables LLMs to effectively identify complex JavaScript vulnerabilities where rule-based SAST tools fail.

claims.text: Our experiments show that LLMs substantially outperform traditional SAST tools on snippet-level vulnerability identification, with a fine-tuned Gemini 1.5 Flash model achieving 60% detection accuracy compared to near-zero performance from rule-based analyzers.

items.title: When Malicious Instructions Persist: Persistent Memory Poisoning Attack on Harness-Based Agents
items.one_liner: PMPA demonstrates how external malicious inputs can poison persistent memory in harness-based agents like Claude Code, triggering attacks across future sessions.
items.summary: Security researchers introduced PMPA (Persistent Memory Poisoning Attack), a technique targeting harness-based LLM agents that integrate persistent cross-session memory. PMPA injects malicious instructions via benign external inputs, prompting the agent to store poisoned context that persists and triggers unauthorized actions or data leakage in subsequent user sessions. Evaluated across OpenClaw and Claude Code, PMPA achieved Cross-session Attack Success Rates of 55.5% and 81.7% respectively, while existing prompt defenses proved largely ineffective once instructions entered persistent storage.

items.bottom_line: LLM agents with persistent memory can be weaponized across sessions via indirect memory poisoning, bypassing standard prompt defenses once data is written to disk.

items.title: The Deception Delta: Adversarial Evaluation of LLM-Based Smart Contract Bytecode Forensics
items.one_liner: Frontier LLMs struggle with smart contract bytecode forensics against adversarial deception, showing a 20% drop in drain detection.
items.summary: Researchers evaluated 22 frontier large language models on their ability to perform blockchain forensics by interpreting unverified smart contract bytecode against adversarially designed deception vectors. Across 8,528 non-refusal runs on 13 purpose-built contracts, adversarial deception reduced drain detection accuracy by 20.0 percentage points compared to controls, with multi-hop call chains and XOR-masked selectors evading detection across nearly all models. The evaluation also uncovered rationalization behavior, where models correctly identified the mechanics of hidden drains but dismissed them as benign under the contract's deceptive framing. Only five models from two providers exceeded 50% detection, demonstrating that current standalone LLMs are unreliable for raw bytecode forensics.
items.bottom_line: Standalone LLMs fail reliably against adversarially disguised smart contract bytecode, frequently falling for deceptive framing despite identifying drain mechanics.

items.title: ZGCM-1: A Fully Open and Extremely Efficient Foundation Model for Math and Agentic Search
items.one_liner: ZGCM-1 is a new open 7B dense foundation model optimized for math and agentic search using internal thinking and tool use.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced ZGCM-1, a fully open 7B dense foundation model trained from scratch with extreme data, system, and algorithmic efficiency. The model tackles the parametric capacity limits of compact models by combining deliberate internal thinking with active external tool use across a 256K context window. Its training pipeline incorporates architectural co-design with gated sliding-window and full attention, a stable FP8 Muon optimizer, and a progressive curriculum transitioning interaction traces into Markov Decision Processes. Evaluations demonstrate that ZGCM-1-7B is competitive on general benchmarks and rivals much larger frontier models on mathematical reasoning and agentic search suites.
items.bottom_line: Compact 7B models can bypass traditional parametric capacity limitations by pairing deliberate internal reasoning with active external tool use across long contexts.

items.title: SkillSecurer: Detecting and Patching Prompt-Injection Vulnerabilities in AI Agent Skills
items.one_liner: SkillSecurer is an agentic security framework that detects and patches prompt-injection vulnerabilities in AI agent skills.
items.summary: AI agent skills often incorporate instructions and scripts that expose them to prompt-injection vulnerabilities and unauthorized manipulations. To mitigate this, researchers have developed SkillSecurer, a fully agentic framework featuring a red agent that generates context-compatible injections across nine threat types and a blue agent that analyses skill packages to produce grounded evidence and patches. In evaluations against popular online skill repositories, SkillSecurer achieved a 100% injection detection rate and uncovered latent security vulnerabilities in over 17% of the examined skills, successfully triggering actual incidents to demonstrate real-world risks.
items.bottom_line: Automated context-aware LLM analysis can effectively uncover and remediate dangerous prompt-injection vulnerabilities hiding within reusable AI agent skills.

items.title: FLoKD: Adaptive Knowledge Distillation for Federated Low-Rank LLM over Wireless Networks
items.one_liner: FLoKD reduces federated LoRA communication overhead by 50-65% by distilling intermediate activations over wireless networks.
items.summary: Federated learning enables collaborative Large Language Model fine-tuning without centralizing raw client data, but bandwidth constraints over wireless networks create significant communication overheads. While Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) reduces trainable parameters and knowledge distillation avoids parameter transmission, transferring full token-level sequence logits incurs high costs. To address these limitations, researchers propose FLoKD, an adaptive knowledge distillation framework that communicates intermediate LoRA activations instead of logits or parameters. Incorporating a transformer block importance scoring mechanism and dataset selection strategies, FLoKD reduces communication overhead by 50-65% across generative language datasets while achieving rapid convergence.
items.bottom_line: Communicating intermediate LoRA activations instead of raw parameters or token logits drastically reduces the communication bottleneck for federated LLM fine-tuning over wireless networks.

items.title: ActGuard: Pre-execution Action Auditing against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
items.one_liner: ActGuard audits LLM agent tool calls pre-execution to defend against indirect prompt injections while maintaining task utility.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed ActGuard, a pre-execution action auditing framework designed to defend LLM agents against indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks without relying on indiscriminate prompt filtering or over-sanitization. Instead of judging external content in isolation, ActGuard predicts expected tool usage to build a local tool prior, performs tool-level contrastive analysis and parameter-level evidence localization, and identifies deviations. A verifier then masks malicious spans and regenerates the action from a sanitized context. Evaluations demonstrate that ActGuard effectively lowers attack success rates while preserving task utility and execution flexibility.
items.bottom_line: Pre-execution action auditing using local tool priors stops indirect prompt injection in LLM agents without degrading task performance.

items.title: PriMobiBench: Characterizing Visual Privacy Leakage in VLM-Driven Mobile GUI Agents
items.one_liner: Evaluating VLM-driven mobile GUI agents reveals severe visual privacy leakage and profiling risks that can be mitigated by masking task-irrelevant UI elements.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced PriMobiBench, the first standardized benchmark for evaluating visual privacy leakage and user profiling risks in Vision-Language Model (VLM)-driven mobile GUI agents. Using their MobiLeak dataset covering execution traces across 16 apps and 2,960 privacy instances, the study reveals that VLMs can directly extract sensitive on-screen data with an 82.5% success rate and infer user profiles from aggregated visual evidence with about 70% success. To mitigate these risks, the authors propose a preprocessing technique that masks privacy-sensitive, task-irrelevant UI elements before cloud processing, successfully cutting profiling success by up to 58% while incurring only an 8% performance loss.

items.title: Detecting and Localizing Segment-Level Poisoning in Multi-Source LLM-Agent Inputs
items.one_liner: ActProbe defends LLM agents against multi-source segment poisoning by analyzing internal MLP activations without modifying the backend model.
items.summary: Modern LLM agents aggregating multi-source inputs are vulnerable to segment-level poisoning attacks where small subsets of sources inject malicious instructions or corrupted evidence. The authors introduce ActProbe, an internal-state framework that projects MLP activations onto a learned poison direction and uses a linear SVM to detect contaminated prompts, combined with BinRoL for efficient segment localization. ActProbe operates without backend model modifications and reduces localization overhead from O(n) exhaustive probing to O(k log n) forward passes. Tested across three datasets, two attacks, and four open-weight LLMs, it achieves a 0.01 false-positive rate and a 0.90 localization F1-score.
items.bottom_line: Detecting prompt injection in multi-source LLM workflows is achievable at low overhead by inspecting internal activation-space poison directions.

items.title: The Stochastic Deputy: Structural Tenant Isolation for Tool-Using LLM Agents
items.one_liner: Removing tenant identifiers from LLM tool schemas and enforcing scope via verified credentials below the agent mitigates the stochastic deputy vulnerability.
items.summary: Multi-tenant LLM tools often accept tenant identifiers and validate them against caller entitlements, creating a stochastic deputy problem where attackers inject instructions to manipulate resource selection. To defend against this, researchers propose removing tenant identity from Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool schemas, binding scope to verified credentials enforced below the agent. In evaluation trials, correctly validated tenant parameters served out-of-scope attempts, whereas removing the parameter prevented tools from expressing unauthorized reads. However, twelve trials still escaped by forging writable scope, and set-valued scope caused a 57x latency ratio under function-wrapped membership predicates unless optimized with index-backed joins.
items.bottom_line: Tenant isolation for LLM agents must rely on cryptographically protected credentials and enforced interfaces rather than model compliance.

items.title: Divide, Consult, Conquer: Capability Laundering Through Aligned LLMs
items.one_liner: Capability laundering allows unaligned models to bypass safety filters by decomposing harmful tasks and consulting aligned frontier models on individual subproblems.
items.summary: Language model safety is typically evaluated per interaction, but researchers demonstrate an attack called capability laundering where an unaligned model splits a harmful task into benign-looking subproblems, queries a stronger aligned model independently on each, and locally combines the answers. Testing GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.8, and Grok-4.3 as consultants to local orchestrators across CyBench, BountyBench, and CBRN requests, the authors found significant capability uplifts. For instance, on CBRN request chains, consultation raised Gemma-4-31B's mean rubric score from 62.3 to 83.1. This exposes a security gap where individual interaction refusals fail to prevent the composition of frontier capabilities.
items.bottom_line: Refusing a harmful task in a single interaction fails to prevent capability laundering through multi-step decomposition and consultation.

items.title: LLM Agent Capabilities Should Follow Task Intent and Context Source
items.one_liner: This provides a robust, policy-driven architecture for developers to restrict LLM agent permissions dynamically, mitigating risks of prompt injection and unauthorized tool usage.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed IntentCap, a framework designed to secure LLM agents by dynamically scoping capabilities based on task intent rather than static sandboxing. The system composes authority from four distinct sources—user intent, workflow instructions, tool schemas, and runtime environment—using a deterministic checker to validate actions before execution. This approach prevents adversarial injection or accidental scope widening by ensuring that different context sources do not share equal influence over an agent's authority.
items.bottom_line: Agent capabilities should be scoped to the specific task intent and validated by a deterministic checker to prevent unauthorized information flow or tool execution.

items.title: 3BB Attacker Used MeshCentral Backdoor for Root Access, Targeted Subscriber Credentials
items.one_liner: Attackers abused MeshCentral backdoors and targeted subscriber credentials inside Thai broadband provider 3BB.
items.summary: Threat intelligence firm Hunt.io revealed that an attacker breached the network of Thai broadband provider 3BB and maintained persistent administrative control using MeshCentral as a hidden backdoor. The intrusion was uncovered via an exposed server containing attacker tools, scripts targeting FortiGate SSL-VPN devices via CVE-2024-21762, and automated password-spraying scripts for internal SSH servers. The primary objective of the campaign was exfiltrating RADIUS databases containing subscriber credentials. The attacker also harvested active VPN certificates connected to infrastructure shared with Jasmine network.
items.bottom_line: Broadband providers must audit internal networks for unauthorized remote management tools and secure VPN gateways against historical exploits.

items.title: ZDI-26-691: Linux Kernel Netlink-based Wireless Configuration Integer Overflow Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A local integer overflow vulnerability in the Linux kernel wireless configuration allows high-privileged attackers to achieve kernel-level code execution.
items.summary: A local privilege escalation vulnerability tracked as ZDI-26-691 has been disclosed in the Linux Kernel Netlink-based Wireless Configuration component. The flaw, caused by an integer overflow during buffer allocation due to improper validation of user-supplied rnr element data, allows local attackers with high-privileged code execution capabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the kernel. Linux has released a security update to address the issue, with the fix available via a designated commit by Linus Torvalds. The vulnerability was reported to the vendor on June 25, 2026, and made public on September 14, 2026.
key_facts: Component: Linux Kernel Netlink-based Wireless Configuration
items.bottom_line: Linux kernel installations are exposed to a Netlink-based integer overflow vulnerability that permits local privilege escalation to kernel context.

items.title: Mind the (Patch) Gap: Multiple Chinese Threat Actors Chain 0-day Exploits in Chrome & Windows
items.one_liner: Chinese threat actors leveraged an active Chrome zero-day and Windows kernel escape exploiting a temporary patch gap.
items.summary: Chinese threat actors UTA0560 and JungleBamboo exploited a multi-stage zero-day exploit chain in Google Chrome and Windows against NGOs in September 2026. The chain leveraged a reflected XSS on a US university website to redirect victims to a Google Chrome type-confusion zero-day in the V8 engine (CVE-2026-85046), combined with a WebAssembly defect (CVE-2026-87491) to escape the V8 sandbox and a Windows kernel vulnerability (CVE-2026-85880) to break out of the browser sandbox. Although CVE-2026-85046 had been fixed upstream in the Chromium codebase on August 4, 2026, a patch gap existed because no stable release of Google Chrome had incorporated the fix at the time of the attacks. Volexity discovered the activity and identified distinct post-exploitation payloads deployed by each actor.
key_facts: CVE-2026-85046: Chrome V8 type confusion zero-day
CVE-2026-85880: Windows kernel privilege escalation / sandbox escape
items.bottom_line: Upstream code fixes do not protect users until a stable browser build is released, exposing a critical patch gap exploited by APT groups.

items.title: Cleartext Credential Recovery in ServiceNow
items.one_liner: ServiceNow's 'Test Credential' feature can be abused to extract cleartext secrets, providing a critical post-exploitation path for red teams.
items.summary: Researchers at SpecterOps have identified a method to retrieve cleartext discovery credentials from ServiceNow instances by abusing the 'CredentialTestAjax' script include. By triggering an AJAX request to the /xmlhttp.do endpoint, an attacker can force the server to return secrets that are otherwise protected from direct UI or API access. This technique allows for the extraction of various credential types, including SSH keys and client secrets, which are stored in the discovery_credentials table. The research highlights a significant post-exploitation vector for attackers who have already gained a foothold in a ServiceNow environment.
items.bottom_line: If you manage ServiceNow instances, you must assume that any user with sufficient privileges to trigger credential tests can potentially extract cleartext secrets from the platform.

items.summary: Two new reporting tools have launched to allow AI agents to whistleblow on misbehaving peers following incidents of cheating and sandbox breakouts. items.summary: Artificial Intelligence Underwriting Company (AIUC), founded by an early Anthropic employee and METR's former COO, has raised a $40 million Series A round led by Ribbit Capital, bringing its total funding to $55 million. The startup provides a third-party audit and verification layer for enterprise AI agents, utilizing a standard called AIUC-1 inspired by SOC 2 compliance. AIUC runs agents through a suite of approximately 5,000 tests covering jailbreaks, hallucinations, and data leaks, ultimately delivering a comprehensive safety report verified by human auditors.
items.bottom_line: Enterprise adoption of AI agents increasingly depends on standardized third-party security audits and compliance certification layers.

items.title: US market today: S&P 500, Nasdaq futures edge lower as oil, yields rise ahead of Fed decision
items.one_liner: US futures drop and 10-year Treasury yields cross 5% ahead of a widely anticipated Federal Reserve rate hike driven by inflation and crude oil surges.
items.summary: US stock futures declined as investors turned cautious ahead of the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision, with rising Treasury yields and elevated crude oil prices reinforcing expectations of a rate hike. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield crossed 5% to reach 5.041%, its highest level since 2007. Meanwhile, Brent crude rose to $108.43 a barrel amid ongoing Middle East disruptions involving Houthi rebel attacks on Saudi infrastructure. Traders have priced in roughly a 90% chance of a quarter-percentage-point rate increase following stubborn inflation data.
items.bottom_line: Soaring Treasury yields and crude oil prices heighten market anxiety as a Federal Reserve rate hike becomes nearly certain.

items.title: NSE IPO Exclusive: Is six months lock-in a challenge? MD-CEO Ashishkumar Chauhan answers
items.one_liner: NSE CEO Ashishkumar Chauhan addresses lock-in concerns ahead of the exchange's upcoming IPO on September 17.
items.summary: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) initial public offering is scheduled to hit the Indian primary market on September 17, 2026, with a price band set between ₹1700 and ₹1785 per share and an estimated grey market premium of 12 percent. Because the offering consists solely of an offer for sale (OFS) with no extra primary stock made available, market observers note that price movement may be limited post-listing, making the six-month lock-in expiration a critical test. However, MD and CEO Ashishkumar Chauhan expressed confidence that institutional and pre--IPO shareholders are financially secure and unlikely to engage in massive sell-offs. Furthermore, the NSE is listing exclusively on the BSE to ensure transparent regulation by a neutral exchange.
key_facts: Price Band: ₹1700 to ₹1785 per equity share
items.bottom_line: The NSE's upcoming IPO features an OFS structure where pre-IPO shareholder behavior after the six-month lock-in will be the primary test for the stock.

items.title: Reversibility-Verified De-identification for Cloud-Local LLM Inference: A Locally Certified Dehydrate-Rehydrate Loop with Layered Assurance (DR-SL)
items.one_liner: DR-SL provides a reversibility-verified de-identification loop for cloud-local LLM inference, balancing zero-leakage data egress with strong semantic utility preservation.
items.summary: Researchers proposed DR-SL (Dehydrate-Rehydrate with Self-Learning loop), a system for cloud-local LLM inference designed to balance sensitive data protection on-device with cloud-grade reasoning utility. The approach formalizes de-identification completeness via Pufferfish semantics and QA-based task-information preservation, employing a local two-branch verifier backed by a hard line, external attacker re-tests, and human fallback. On a worst-case task-coupled benchmark, the loop reduced leakage from 0.457 to 0.304 while achieving zero literal leakage at egress across 160 instances. A mixed-coupling benchmark demonstrated that the safe operating point automatically released 67.5% of instances at zero measured leakage, outperforming placeholder and selective-LDP approaches.
items.bottom_line: Certified dehydration-rehydration frameworks can successfully eliminate data leakage at cloud egress without sacrificing task utility.

items.title: Fusing Spectral Signatures and Activation Clustering for Backdoor Detection in Healthcare Imaging Models: Method, Implementation, and Evaluation
items.one_liner: Combining spectral signatures and activation clustering yields AUROC >= 0.99 for backdoor detection in medical imaging models.
items.summary: Researchers proposed a fused backdoor detection pipeline for healthcare imaging machine learning models that combines spectral signature analysis and activation clustering into a single per-sample poisoning score and model agreement statistic. Evaluated on a public medical imaging benchmark, the fused detector achieved an AUROC >= 0.99 at every nonzero poisoning rate (1%, 5%, 10%). However, evaluation on CIFAR-10 revealed joint failure modes where individual component detectors degraded, illustrating limitations when translating detection baselines across domains.
items.bottom_line: Score-level fusion of spectral signatures and activation clustering provides robust backdoor detection for healthcare imaging models.

claims.text: On the medical benchmark, the fused detector reaches AUROC >= 0.99 at every nonzero poisoning rate tested.

items.title: LLM-Enhanced Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Unified Electric Vehicles-Charging Station-Grid Optimization in Public Charging Systems
items.one_liner: A research paper introduces an LLM-guided multi-agent reinforcement learning system that optimizes EV charging grids while cutting training time by 70%.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed an LLM-enhanced Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework designed to optimize electric vehicle charging across grids, vehicles, and charging stations. The architecture uses an LLM to interpret high-dimensional IoT sensor data, extract physically meaningful features, and dynamically balance conflicting objectives such as charging speed, station profit, and grid load. Experimental results demonstrate that the framework achieves higher market efficiency while reducing model training times by over 70%.

items.title: Confuse the Model, Control the Flow: Understanding and Mitigating Privacy Leakage from LLM Agents with Information Flow Control
items.one_liner: Researchers exposed systemic privacy leaks in LLM personal agents and developed FLOWSEAL, an external flow-control defense reducing leak rates to near zero.
items.summary: Security researchers have highlighted critical privacy vulnerabilities in LLM-based personal agents where backend prompt-level safeguards fail against non-injection interaction attacks. The paper demonstrates three novel attack patterns—Collaborative Workspace Lure, Semantic Obfuscation, and Channel Decoupling—that bypass conventional system prompt defenses by splitting or disguising data extraction. To counter this, the authors introduce FLOWSEAL, an external tool-level interceptor that enforces information flow control lattices and data provenance, dropping leak rates from 52.2% to 0.5% on tested benchmarks.
key_facts: Leak rate reduction: 52.2% to 0.5% against Collaborative Workspace Lure
Novel attack types: Collaborative Workspace Lure, Semantic Obfuscation, Channel Decoupling
items.bottom_line: Prompt-based agent guardrails fail against semantic and multi-channel extraction, requiring external tool-level information flow control like FLOWSEAL to prevent sensitive data leaks.

claims.text: Three novel attacks bypass prompt defenses without prompt injection: Collaborative Workspace Lure, Semantic Obfuscation, and Channel Decoupling.
claims.support_span: We demonstrate this against existing defenses with three new attacks that require only ordinary agent interaction and no prompt injection: Collaborative Workspace Lure reframes an extraction attempt as collaborative work; Semantic Obfuscation Attack induces disclosure through omission rather than through anything the agent writes; and Channel Decoupling Attack splits the extraction request and the disclosure across independent channels.

claims.text: The FLOWSEAL defense reduces leak rates from 52.2% to 0.5% against Collaborative Workspace Lures by intercepting tool calls outside the LLM context.
claims.support_span: Evaluated across three benchmarks, five prompt-based baselines, and eight attacks, including a real agent executing live tool calls through MCP, FLOWSEAL reduces leak rates to near zero (e.g., 52.2% to 0.5% against Collaborative Workspace Lure) while preserving task utility, regardless of the underlying LLM backend.

items.title: LoRA Fine-Tuned Models for Control Systems Course Q\&A: A Multidimensional Evaluation of Model Scale and Rank Effects
items.one_liner: LoRA fine-tuning on Qwen2.5 models improves pedagogical answer formatting and text similarity for control systems course Q&A.
items.summary: Researchers evaluated LoRA fine-tuning on Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct using a dataset of 360 conversation pairs for a Linear Control Systems university course. Testing LoRA ranks r=4, 8, and 16, they found that fine-tuning improved both text similarity and structured-output format stability. The 7B-r16 configuration achieved the highest ROUGE-L (0.4093) and BERTScore-F1 (0.8643), though metrics reflect textual formatting rather than mathematical correctness.
items.bottom_line: LoRA rank and model scale enhance structural consistency in LLM-generated technical course responses.

items.title: HYDRA: Quantifying Botnet Resource Thresholds for Efficient Link-Flooding Attacks on LEO Satellite Networks
items.one_liner: HYDRA optimizes botnet resource thresholds for efficient link-flooding attacks against LEO satellite constellations.
items.summary: Researchers introduced HYDRA, a modeling and optimization framework that formulates link-flooding attacks (LFAs) on Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks as botnet minimization problems. HYDRA quantifies network resilience by calculating the minimum active bots and traffic required to disrupt target geographic areas. Under matched stealth constraints, HYDRA achieves equivalent targeted disruption to ICARUS while utilizing 34% fewer bots and 23% less aggregate traffic, maintaining over 97% success as network topologies evolve.
items.bottom_line: HYDRA demonstrates that LEO satellite constellations are vulnerable to highly efficient link-flooding attacks using minimized botnet resources.

items.title: PIDS-Bench: Evaluating Prompt-Injection Detectors Under Over-Defense, Obfuscation, and Distribution Shift
items.one_liner: PIDS-Bench multi-axis evaluation reveals that prompt-injection detectors suffer from high false-positive rates on external benign security text.
items.summary: Researchers presented PIDS-Bench, a frozen multi-axis benchmark evaluating prompt-injection detectors across in-distribution data, obfuscated attacks, distribution shifts, and hard-benign prompts mimicking injection structure. Evaluating seven detectors revealed that aggregate F1 scores conceal severe false-positive operational costs: no internal detector achieved F1 >= 0.95 alongside a hard-benign false positive rate <= 0.10 on external security-adjacent corpora, exhibiting provenance-sensitive over-defense.
items.bottom_line: Prompt-injection detectors frequently over-defend and fail external benign stress distributions despite high in-distribution F1 scores.

items.title: Automating Attack Graph Construction for Agentic Pentesting. Towards Neuro-Symbolic Vulnerability Hunting
items.one_liner: This pipeline bridges the gap between raw scanner output and symbolic attack path reasoning, improving the reliability of agentic pentesting.
items.summary: A new semi-automated pipeline integrates security scanner findings (Trivy, Semgrep, Nmap) into symbolic logic frameworks like MulVAL to generate structured attack graphs for agentic pentesting. By translating scanner evidence into Datalog predicates, the system allows LLM-based agents to reason about attack paths with auditability. Evaluation on 54 web-security tasks showed a 53.7% mean ground-truth vulnerability coverage, providing a practical, runtime-feasible method for graph-guided security testing.

items.bottom_line: Integrating symbolic reasoning into agentic pentesting workflows provides a structured, auditable way to map attack paths from scanner data.

items.title: GeoSkill:Experience-Driven Hierarchical Skill Learning with Collaborative Revision forGeospatialAgents
items.one_liner: GeoSkill introduces a structured hierarchical memory framework that helps AI agents reliably distill geospatial planning and tool-use experience.
items.summary: Geospatial agents struggle with recurring analytical tasks because they lack effective mechanisms to distill prior execution experience into reusable procedural knowledge. To resolve this, researchers propose GeoSkill, a hierarchical skill learning framework that separates task-planning experience from tool-level invocation constraints using a Hierarchical Skill Bank and a Collaborative Trace-driven Skill Revision mechanism. The framework employs Judge, Critic, and Refiner roles to collaboratively localize defects and modify skills without relying on error-prone LLM self-reflection. Experiments on EarthBench and ThinkGeo show that GeoSkill improves both end-to-end task accuracy and tool-execution reliability.
items.bottom_line: Structuring agent memory and separating planning from tool constraints via collaborative trace review significantly improves geospatial task execution accuracy.

claims.text: GeoSkill comprises two core components: (i) a Hierarchical Skill Bank (HSB)... and (ii) a Collaborative Trace-driven Skill Revision (CTSR) mechanism...
claims.support_span: GeoSkill comprises two core components: (i) a Hierarchical Skill Bank (HSB), consisting of a Planning Skill Bank and a Tool Skill Bank, which respectively distill high-level task-planning experience and tool usage constraints, enabling structured representation and cross-task reuse of historical execution experience; and (ii) a Collaborative Trace-driven Skill Revision (CTSR) mechanism, where Judge, Critic, and Refiner collaboratively perform error identification, skill-level defect localization, and targeted modification, preventing misattributed and unreliable revisions from polluting the skill bank.

items.title: Surprising Effectiveness of Self-Demonstrations in Enhancing Schema-Ontology Mapping with LLMs
items.one_liner: A new neuro-symbolic, self-demonstration approach improves LLM-based schema-to-ontology mapping by 25 F1 percentage points.
items.summary: Integrating heterogeneous relational databases into a centralized ontology remains challenging due to semantic heterogeneity and abstraction gaps, and naive or one-shot LLM prompts perform poorly on these tasks. The authors propose a self-demonstration-driven approach combining neuro-symbolic task decomposition—where symbolic constraints structure the search space—with automatically generated, pattern-guided, dependency-aware demonstrations. Evaluated on challenging RODI benchmark scenarios, this approach achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming traditional techniques and baseline LLM methods by 25 percentage points in F1 score. Ablation studies confirm the specific benefits of pattern-guided self-demonstrations and neuro-symbolic task decomposition.
items.bottom_line: Combining neuro-symbolic task decomposition with pattern-guided self-demonstrations overcomes fundamental LLM limitations in schema-ontology mapping, achieving state-of-the-art benchmark performance.

items.title: RAPID: A Real-Time Defense Against Unauthorized Model Distillation for Text-to-Image Services
items.one_liner: RAPID provides real-time protection against unauthorized text-to-image model distillation by embedding disruptive latent defenses directly into shared VAE decoders.
items.summary: Diffusion-based text-to-image models are vulnerable to unauthorized black-box output-based distillation where attackers train substitute models using queried prompt-image pairs. While sample-wise perturbation defenses add heavy computational latency, integrating defenses into shared VAE decoders has suffered from limited latent shifts and poor objective reachability. To counter this, researchers propose RAPID, a self-referenced latent maximization framework with reconstruction-guided color regularization that introduces consistently disruptive effects across training samples without external dependencies. Experiments show RAPID successfully degrades unauthorized substitute generation quality while preserving original service fidelity.
items.bottom_line: Self-referenced latent maximization in shared VAE decoders effectively blocks unauthorized model distillation without degrading online text-to-image generation performance.

claims.text: To overcome this limitation, we propose RAPID, a self-referenced latent maximization framework that removes external dependencies and encourages the same model update to induce consistently disruptive effects across training samples, thereby improving reachability.

items.title: Root-Cause Attribution Is a Search Problem: Continual Search for Long-Horizon Agent Failures
items.one_liner: Continual Search transforms agent failure diagnosis from a one-shot judgment into an iterative search process, significantly boosting LLM root-cause attribution accuracy.
items.summary: Automated root-cause attribution for long-horizon AI agent failures suffers from low diagnostic accuracy because relevant error evidence is sparse and distributed across massive execution logs. Traditional one-shot LLM judgments tend to settle on early plausible diagnoses while ignoring critical evidence in longer execution traces. To overcome this, researchers introduce Continual Search, an iterative framework that prompts diagnostic models to continue searching for unresolved evidence over successive turns. Evaluated across multiple benchmarks including a new testbed called MegaRCA-Mix, Continual Search significantly improves attribution performance, raising GPT-5.5's F1 score by over 40% and proving that systematic search strategies outperform raw model scale.
key_facts: F1 score improvement: over 40% (0.349 to 0.498 for GPT-5.5)
items.bottom_line: Iterative search mechanisms solve the sparse evidence problem in long-horizon agent logs, enabling lower-tier models to surpass higher-tier ones in root-cause diagnosis.

items.title: Identity Is More Than Recall: A Benchmark for Persistent Identity in Deployed AI Agents
items.one_liner: PAI-Bench is a new benchmark for evaluating persistent identity fidelity and behavioral enactment in AI agents.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced PAI-Bench, a provider-neutral benchmark designed to evaluate persistent identity fidelity in deployed AI agents against versioned identity contracts. The framework decouples recall, composition, behavioral enactment, resistance, persistence, lineage, and role-conditioned updates while maintaining external scoring oracles. Evaluations across 1,536 retained responses revealed significant prompt-dependent component selection and sensitivity to startup cues. Furthermore, tests demonstrated evaluator sensitivity differences across model architectures like Claude and Astra.
items.bottom_line: AI agents exhibit prompt-dependent identity expression and sensitivity to startup cues that require specialized benchmarks beyond simple recall.

items.title: IBBench-Light: A Paired Evaluation of Task-Conditioned Responses to External Directives
items.one_liner: IBBench-Light evaluates LLM task-conditioned responses and highlights how stopping policies dictate exact-contract success.
items.summary: Researchers introduce IBBench-Light to evaluate task-conditioned responses to external records, testing whether models can execute a procedure or read text from the same record using twelve semantic bases and 144 matched pairs. items.bottom_line: Model compliance with paired output contracts depends heavily on generation stopping parameters rather than standalone task prompts alone.

items.title: AutoTailor: Automatic, User-Aligned Capability Selection and Adaptation for Web Agents
items.one_liner: AutoTailor optimizes web agent performance and token costs by automatically selecting and dynamically adapting user-aligned Model Context Protocol APIs.
items.summary: Web agents utilizing large tool collections often suffer from redundancy, high costs, and poor semantic alignment with user demand. To solve this, researchers propose AutoTailor, a meta-agentic framework that converts web trajectories into parameterized Model Context Protocol APIs, filters them using quality and usage likelihood filters, and dynamically adjusts the active API set during deployment. In evaluations on WebArena tasks, offline and dynamic filtering reduced an initial pool of 1,283 APIs down to a compact set of 33, which improved correctness to 90.6% while cutting average request-token costs by 57.8% and latency by 29.4%.
items.bottom_line: Filtering and dynamically managing tool inventories for web agents substantially reduces operational latency and token costs while maintaining high task correctness.

items.title: Toward Self-Adaptive Physical AI: Can LLM Agents Manage Long-Horizon Physical Tasks?
items.one_liner: Zero-shot LLM agent frameworks demonstrate strong adaptability in managing long-horizon physical tasks across changing environments.
items.summary: Researchers explored the feasibility of building self-adaptive physical AI agents capable of managing long-horizon physical tasks in a zero-shot manner without human intervention. By designing a multi-agent framework combining planning, tool calling, observation, and verification, the authors evaluated LLM agents against reinforcement learning (RL) agents on agricultural tasks under varying weather patterns. Results showed that zero-shot LLM agents achieved comparable outcomes under normal conditions and adapted significantly better than RL agents when evaluated under shifted environmental conditions.
items.bottom_line: Multi-agent LLM frameworks can successfully manage long-term physical tasks and adapt to environmental shifts better than traditional reinforcement learning agents.
