items.title: LabAgent: Customize Any Research Hubs for Scientific Discoveries Using AI Agents
items.one_liner: A new framework, LabAgent, helps preserve and reproduce laboratory research pipelines despite student and staff turnover.
items.summary: To address the loss of research continuity caused by staff turnover in scientific laboratories, researchers have proposed LabAgent, a reproduce and discovery harness designed for a lab's ongoing work. The agent uses two mechanisms to ensure all skills execute and verify properly while recording corrective methods and experiences to avoid recurring errors. Tested across domains such as drug property prediction, biomedical problem analysis, protein variant effect prediction, and statistical genetics, LabAgent outperformed commercial generalist agents. It effectively integrates and expands laboratory knowledge to maintain long-term research capabilities.
items.bottom_line: LabAgent offers labs an automated way to preserve methodology and prevent institutional knowledge loss from personnel turnover.

items.title: Token Efficient Task Execution via Application Behavior Modeling for Web Agents
items.one_liner: OdoBot reduces web agent token costs significantly by modeling application behavior from past demonstrations.
items.summary: To combat the rising cost of processing tokens in web-agent automation, researchers have introduced OdoBot, a novel web-agent architecture. items.title: Vibe Patenting: Evaluating LLM Judges for Professional Patent-Drafting Agents
items.one_liner: LLM judges improve patent-drafting agent outputs through iterative feedback, allowing low-reasoning models to approach expensive high-reasoning performance.
items.summary: Researchers studied the reliability of LLM judges for professional patent-drafting agents through a testbed called Vibe Patenting, where an independently-invoked judge evaluates drafts and gives structured feedback for iterative revision. The evaluation shows that judge-guided revision consistently improves quality and enables a low-reasoning agent to approach the performance of a much more expensive high-reasoning agent. Validation against independent professional patent attorney evaluations reveals meaningful but metric-dependent agreement and systematic calibration differences. These findings demonstrate both the utility and limits of LLM judges in complex professional workflows.
items.bottom_line: LLM judges can effectively guide complex professional agent workflows, though their agreement with human experts remains metric-dependent.

items.title: Safety as a Constraint: Fine-Tuning a LLM Recommender to Explain Itself
items.one_liner: Fine-tuning a recommender LLM with constrained GRPO enables it to generate safe, faithful explanations without losing recommendation accuracy.
items.summary: Traditional recommender systems predict user interactions without explaining why items are suggested, while using frontier models for explanations adds latency and cost. Researchers trained a recommender LLM to generate personalized, faithful, and non-harmful explanations based on watching history at a video streaming service. Using two LLM-judge reward models and constrained GRPO, the fine-tuned model's all-criteria pass rate increased from 0.649 to 0.956 under internal judges and from 0.677 to 0.931 under independent judges, without affecting recommendation performance.

items.title: A Hybrid Agentic AI Framework for Intelligent Supply Chain Analytics
items.one_liner: A hybrid multi-agent AI framework improves supply chain analytics accuracy while cutting token usage by fourfold.
items.summary: Efficient supply chain analytics requires heterogeneous expertise across data engineering, operations research, and business logic. To bridge this gap, researchers proposed an agentic framework where a coordinator agent interprets user intent and delegates sub-tasks to specialized domain agents. Evaluated on multi-echelon inventory management operations, the multi-agent system achieved 90% accuracy while reducing input token usage by roughly fourfold compared to single-agent baselines. This architecture combines exploratory analysis and deterministic workflows for scalable decision-support.
items.bottom_line: Multi-agent orchestration can handle complex supply chain analytics tasks efficiently by dividing labor between specialized domain agents.

items.title: SAILOR: Solver-Assisted Interactive LLM-based Optimization Recovery
items.one_liner: SAILOR uses solver-guided LLM interactions to query users for missing numerical constraints in optimization problem descriptions.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced SAILOR (Solver-Assisted Interactive LLM-based Optimization Recovery), a proof-of-concept system designed to fix incomplete or vague natural-language descriptions of optimization problems. When numerical requirements such as costs, capacities, and demands are missing, SAILOR detects the unsupported choices, prioritizes targeted follow-up questions using solver-derived uncertainty estimates, and interactively updates the optimization model. Evaluated across 1,723 instances from seven masked benchmarks using an idealized ground-truth simulator, the system achieved exact objective-value agreements ranging from 27.0% to 87.6% while asking an average of 1.4 to 5.7 questions per instance. However, these controlled tests do not reflect performance with human users or general structural model repairs.

items.bottom_line: SAILOR successfully automates the detection and interactive resolution of missing numerical constraints in optimization models using solver feedback.

items.title: Do Not Restart: Residual Completion for Stateful Agent Handoffs
items.one_liner: Commitment-Frontier Residual Completion reduces stateful agent handoff costs while preserving completed progress and pending obligations.
items.summary: Stateful agent handoffs require transferring control across models while preserving accepted choices, realized effects, and pending obligations. The authors formulate this challenge as commitment-constrained residual completion and introduce Commitment-Frontier Residual Completion (CFRC). CFRC enforces strict rules including target-before-proposal and live-evidence-before-success by freezing residual contracts and linking continuations into evidence graphs. Across five environments and two same-provider model pairs, CFRC achieved macro accuracy comparable to full-task agents while incurring only 22.0% to 34.6% of their inference cost.
items.bottom_line: Enforcing commitment-constrained residual completion during agent handoffs dramatically lowers inference costs without sacrificing execution accuracy.

items.title: Enhancing Event Candidate Acquisition for Event Linking
items.one_liner: MACE uses specialized LLM agents to refine event structures and improve candidate acquisition for event linking models.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced MACE (Multi-Agent Candidate Event acquisition), a method designed to enhance event linking by refining event structures before mapping event mentions in text to knowledge base entries. MACE employs evidence-specialized LLM agents to independently gather time, location, participant, and event-type evidence, exposes intermediate queries to candidate lookup tools, and uses a coordinator to revise the evidence set. Evaluations across two event linking benchmarks demonstrated that integrating MACE consistently improves accuracy across different event-linking models without requiring modifications to the core models themselves.
items.bottom_line: Integrating MACE's multi-agent evidence acquisition pipeline consistently boosts event linking accuracy without modifying underlying models.

items.title: JaxAHT: A JAX-Based Library for Ad Hoc Teamwork
items.one_liner: JaxAHT is a JAX-accelerated open-source library that speeds up Ad Hoc Teamwork research by 95x over PyTorch frameworks.
items.summary: JaxAHT is an open-source, JAX-based library designed to accelerate and standardize Ad Hoc Teamwork (AHT) research, where agents must coordinate with novel partners without prior coordination. Leveraging JAX hardware acceleration and massive parallelization, JaxAHT delivers approximately a 95x wall-clock speedup over PyTorch counterparts while providing a unified framework for teammate generation, ego agent training, and evaluation. The authors also contributed an evaluation teammate suite across Level-Based Foraging, Overcooked, and Hanabi, demonstrating through large-scale benchmarks that agent modeling provides the most benefit in role-based scenarios.
items.bottom_line: JAX-based hardware acceleration can overcome the prohibitive computational costs of standardizing multi-agent ad hoc teamwork research.

items.one_liner: Linux kernel CVE-2026-43040 exposes uninitialized IPv6 Neighbour Discovery memory to privileged local attackers.

items.title: Generating running routes with GPT-6 Astra and ChatGPT Work
items.one_liner: An AI agent successfully generated localized running routes using OpenStreetMap data, but opaque chat thread compaction blocked access to its underlying Python execution code.
items.summary: Simon Willison used GPT-6 Astra (Max) via ChatGPT Work to successfully generate 5K and 10K running routes looping from his home using OpenStreetMap data via Nominatim and Overpass. The tool ran for 27 minutes and produced embedded visualizations alongside downloadable GPX and GeoJSON files. However, thread compaction in the ChatGPT UI prevented him from retrieving the underlying Python code that the agent had executed, highlighting a lack of execution transparency. The generated maps utilized D3 loaded from an allow-listed CDN supported by the system's visualize skill.
items.bottom_line: AI agent tools that rely on automatic thread compaction must preserve pre-compacted text and expose it via tool calls to maintain execution transparency.

items.summary: Japan's centenarian population has surpassed 100,000 for the first time, reaching a record 107,677 individuals, with women representing 88% of the total. Accurate dosing is important because too little heparin can lead to clotting, while too much can cause excessive bleeding. The research team, led by Shanmugaraju Sankarasekaran and research scholar Noushija M.K., developed fluorescent chemosensors to detect heparin levels. The new method uses fluorescence instead of the clotting-time measurements used in existing monitoring methods.
